You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure is triggered when HelpFormatter tries to render the option list with a narrow width such that the computed indent for wrapped lines (nextLineTabStop) leaves no space for any text.

Step-by-step:
- The test configures a single option “-x,--extralongarg” with description “This description is Long.”, a width of 22, leftPad = 0, and descPad = 5.
- In HelpFormatter.renderOptions(), the prefix for the option is built as “-x,--extralongarg” (length 17). With descPad = 5, nextLineTabStop is computed as max + descPad = 17 + 5 = 22.
- The full line passed to renderWrappedText() is the 22-character prefix/padding plus the description, and the formatter width is also 22.
- HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText() first computes a wrap position via findWrapPos(). For the first line, findWrapPos() returns 21 (it wraps at the last space before or at column 22, which is within the 5-space descPad).
- After appending the first line, renderWrappedText() checks:
  if (nextLineTabStop >= width) { throw new IllegalStateException("Total width is less than the width of the argument and indent - no room for the description"); }
  Since nextLineTabStop == 22 and width == 22, this condition is true and an IllegalStateException is thrown.
- This exception was introduced to prevent a prior infinite loop when the indent consumed all available width (as per the current bug report). However, in this test the expected behavior is to ignore (reduce) the indent when it would leave no room for wrapped text, not to throw.

Why the infinite loop bug existed:
- The wrapping loop in renderWrappedText() repeatedly prefixes subsequent lines with nextLineTabStop spaces:
  text = padding + text.substring(pos).trim();
  If nextLineTabStop >= width, there’s no space for content after the indent, and findWrapPos() could keep returning a position that does not advance the text, causing an infinite loop. The guard (nextLineTabStop >= width) was added to break that loop by throwing.

Why this test fails now:
- The guard is too strict for legitimate content: when nextLineTabStop equals width (not greater), the formatter could still proceed by ignoring the indent for wrapped lines (as the test name implies: “Indent Ignored”), but the current code throws unconditionally for equality too.
- In short, with width 22 and nextLineTabStop 22, HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText() throws instead of wrapping the description with the indent ignored, causing the test to fail.

Conclusion:
- The failure stems from HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText()’s “anti-infinite-loop” guard throwing when nextLineTabStop >= width. In the scenario exercised by the test, it should instead ignore the indent (or otherwise reduce it) for wrapped lines to allow progress, thereby preventing both the infinite loop and the unnecessary exception.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
